It gives understanding to the simple.” (web:Ps.119.130) (check_web_quotes GREEN, 11 quotes, 0 flags). Confidence high is calibrated: an 8-verse single-letter run with a byte-verified letter change on the closing side is the strongest tier-1 warrant this book offers. One observation, not filed as a defect because the structured field is correct: the device_notes phrase 'kept apart as two parents rather than merged into one row' misuses 'parents' -- parent_psalm is 119 for both the NUN and PE rows under the one-parent-per-psalm rule, so these are two rows under one parent.

The forward seam is byte-real: MT Ps.119.145-Ps.119.152 opens on U+05E7 HEBREW LETTER QOF throughout, 1 distinct letter, so the change at Ps.119.144|Ps.119.145 is a letter change and not an inference. Ps 119 being identity, the row's plain web:/oshb: pairs need no offset and none is asserted. WEB quotes verbatim, 2 of 2 checked: “You are righteous, Yahweh. Your judgments are upright.” (web:Ps.119.137) and “Your promises have been thoroughly tested, and your servant loves them.” (web:Ps.119.140). Disclosure audit: MT Ps.119.137-Ps.119.144 carries 0 selah, 0 paseq, 0 ketiv/qere and 0 seg-layer objects in pmarks_Ps.json, so no disclosure was owed. Span, unit_type, parent, tiling and refs mirroring are clean (check_tiling GREEN over Ps.119.129-Ps.119.176, 48/48 verses, 0 gaps and 0 overlaps; check_refs_mirror GREEN). The boundary warrant is sound and I do not contest the span. What fails is a distributional claim in device_notes that no sweep supports: it attaches righteousness vocabulary to the stanza's 8 verses, and the root is present in only 4 of them. That is a count-object defect under the campaign's name-the-object-then-count rule, filed at low because it is texture disclosure and leaves the acrostic warrant untouched. Confidence high is otherwise calibrated.

The span and its warrant are byte-sound and I do not contest them: MT Ps.119.153-Ps.119.160 shows 1 distinct opening letter across all 8 verses, U+05E8 HEBREW LETTER RESH, and the forward side MT Ps.119.161-Ps.119.168 shows 1 distinct opening letter, U+05E9 HEBREW LETTER SHIN, so the seam at Ps.119.160|Ps.119.161 is a real letter change. רְאֵֽה collates BYTE against oshb:Ps.119.153 and שָׂ֭רִים collates BYTE against oshb:Ps.119.161, both complete first tokens, 2 of 2. Every one of your righteous ordinances endures forever.” (web:Ps.119.160). The paseq claim checks out against the inventory rather than against lore: pmarks_Ps.json lists paseq at MT Ps.119.156 and that is the only paseq seg in MT Ps.119.153-Ps.119.160 (1 of 5 in the whole psalm), the row types it as seg layer and carries the mandated single-witness disclosure, and it does not treat it as a driver. The defect is a disclosure gap on the forward-seam quote: the row lifts pointed Hebrew out of MT Ps.119.161, which is a ketiv/qere verse, without any K/Q disclosure. Filed low -- the quoted token is not the K/Q token and the warrant survives -- but the rule is verse-scoped and the cure is a shared-seam edit. One further observation not filed: the rationale calls web:Ps.119.157 'its own count of persecutors', where WEB reads “Many are my persecutors and my adversaries.” (web:Ps.119.157) and the MT has a quantifier, not an enumeration; the reference and the content are right and no digit-bearing claim is made, so this is loose wording rather than a count-object breach. reviews.reasoning: This was the row with the most to check and it survives most of it. The acrostic claim is exact once the tier is read carefully: MT Ps.119.161-Ps.119.168 carries 1 distinct opening letter at skeleton tier, U+05E9 HEBREW LETTER SHIN, across all 8 verses. At BYTE tier the diacritic splits 3 sin-dot verses (MT Ps.119.161, Ps.119.162, Ps.119.166, U+05C2) against 5 shin-dot verses (MT Ps.119.163, Ps.119.164, Ps.119.165, Ps.119.167, Ps.119.168, U+05C1); ps_lib.skeleton() strips U+05C1 and U+05C2 because its POINTS class spans U+0591-U+05C7, so the row's phrase locating the shared letter 'in the OSHB skeleton, byte-verified' is precise rather than sloppy, and device_notes discloses the two readings and names the shared consonant, not either reading singly, as the driver. That is the correct handling of the one stanza in this psalm where a naive byte claim would have been false, and I want it recorded as verified rather than assumed. שָׂ֭רִים collates BYTE against oshb:Ps.119.161 and תִּקְרַ֤ב collates BYTE against oshb:Ps.119.169, both complete first tokens; the forward seam is byte-real, MT Ps.119.169-Ps.119.176 carrying 1 distinct opening letter, U+05EA HEBREW LETTER TAV. WEB quotes verbatim, 2 of 2 checked, “Princes have persecuted me without a cause, but my heart stands in awe of your words.” (web:Ps.119.161) and “I rejoice at your word, as one who finds great plunder.” (web:Ps.119.162). The lexical echo the row asserts is real on the bytes and I do not contest it -- only the position it assigns to it. Two defects filed: the undisclosed ketiv/qere at MT Ps.119.161, which matters more here than at the closing row because this row also quotes the WEB rendering whose final phrase follows the ketiv against the pointed qere the row quotes from; and the misplacement of web:Ps.119.23 at the GIMEL stanza's close. Neither touches the span, the unit_type or the parent, and confidence high remains calibrated on the acrostic warrant.

Cure is one edit shared with the row closing at Ps.119.160, installed on both sides of that seam in the same pass.
